meta.question: Is there a Small Claims Court?

question: Is there a Small Claims Court?

answers:
Yes, there is a Small Claims Court. Small Claims cases are heard at the Gordon D. Schaber Sacramento County Courthouse and during Night Court sessions at the Carol Miller Justice Center. Night Court services are available on the second Wednesday of each month from 4:00 p.m. to 6:15 p.m. Small Claims trials are conducted in person and via video during these Night Court sessions. 
The Small Claims Court provides a special venue for resolving disputes quickly and inexpensively. The rules are simple, and the hearings are informal. Attorneys are not permitted to represent parties during the proceedings, but you may consult a lawyer for advice before attending Small Claims Court. In this court, disputes are settled in a fair, swift, and cost-effective manner.

history.content: When are night court services available and what types of matters are heard in there?

Night Court services at the Carol Miller Justice Center are available on the 2nd Wednesday of each month from 4:00 p.m. to 6:15 p.m. If the second Wednesday of the month is a court holiday, Night Court will be held on the 2nd Thursday of that same month. During Night Court, Traffic arraignments and Small Claims trials are heard in person and via video. Mediation and Advisory Services for Small Claims and Unlawful Detainer matters are available in person and via video utilizing Zoom. However, please note that interpreter services are not currently available during the Night Court hours.
The Gordon D. Schaber Sacramento County Courthouse

The Gordon D. Schaber Sacramento County Courthouse houses the main administrative offices of the court, as well as containing trial courtrooms, the department of the Presiding Judge, and the general civil and criminal case processing support units.
The Hall of Justice Building in the immediate vicinity of the Gordon D. Schaber Sacramento County Courthouse also provides court services. Located on the second floor at 813 6th Street are Departments 53 and 54, hearing general civil law and motion matters. Located at 813 6th Street, first floor, is Department 59 where general civil settlement conferences are heard.

evidence.text:
What Is Small Claims Court?
Small claims court is a special court where disputes are resolved quickly and inexpensively. The rules are simple and informal. The person who sues is the plaintiff. The person who is sued is the defendant. In small claims court, you may ask a lawyer for advice before you go to court, but you cannot have a lawyer in court.
Your claim cannot be for more than $10,000.00. If you have a claim for more than this amount, you may file a limited civil case, or you may sue in the small claims court and give up your right to the amount over $10,000.00. You cannot, however, file more than two cases in small claims court for more than $2,500.00 each during a calendar year.
Who Can File a Claim?

Small claims in California | California Courts | Self Help Guide
Generally, you can only sue for up to $12,500 in small claims court (or up to $6,250 if you’re a business). You can ask a lawyer for advice before you go to court, but you can't have one with you in court.
Special rules for COVID-19 rental debt cases in small claims
Starting November 1, 2021, you can sue or be sued for COVID-19 rental debt in small claims. If you are suing a tenant for COVID-19 rental debt, you can sue for more than $12,500. 
Get more information about COVID-19 rental debt cases in small claims. Learn more
COVID-19 rental debt is unpaid rent due from March 1, 2020 to September 30, 2021, and any other money owed, like parking fees, under a rental agreement.Get more information
You can get general information in the COVID-19 Rental Debt in Small Claims Court (form SC-500-INFO).
If you want to sue a tenant for COVID-19 rental debt, get step-by-step instructions on how to start a case.
